Misc. 339/40
Chengtu Road
Sept. 13, 40.
Visit of Japanese to the 2nd Branch Kiangsu High Court, Wei Hai Wei
Road.
/// and D. I. Hill.

Sir,
At 3.15 p.m. 13-9-40, C.U.C. 213, C.P.C.s 3844 and
3744, on duty at the 2nd Branch of the Kiangsu High
Court, No. 10/150 Wei Hai Wei Road, reported that at
2.50 p.m. 13-9-40 a party of some eight Japanese accom-
panied by a male Chinese visited the High Court, they
remained on the premises for about five minutes and
left in three m/cars. The male Chinese who apparently
was acting as escort to the party was identified as
Mr. T.J. Lee, Assistant Municipal Advocate.
The undersigned communicated with Supt. Shellewell,
Liaison Officer Municipal Advocates Office, in order to
obtain further verification of the reported presence
of the representative of the Municipal Advocates Depart-
ment. The latter mentioned officer after conferring
with Mr. R.T. Fryer, jr. Municipal Advocate, informed the
undersigned that the Japanese were Judicial Officers
from Tokyo, Japan and a tour of the Chinese Courts had
been arranged through Mr. C. Akagi, Special Deputy Com-
missioner. The undersigned immediately informed the
D. O. "A" who stated that he had no information on the
subject.
At 3.25 p.m. 13-9-40, a telephone message was re-
ceived from the Intelligence Officer, U.S.M.C. reporting
the visit of the Japanese to the High Court and asking
if the S.M.Police had any information on the subject,
the former was informed of the result of Police enquiries.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
D. I.

杂项 339/40
成都路
1940年9月13日。
日本人访问位于威海卫路的江苏高等法院第二分院。
/// 及 D. I. Hill。

先生，
1940年9月13日下午3时15分，在威海卫路10/150号江苏高等法院第二分院执勤的华捕警长（C.U.C.）213号、华捕巡警（C.P.C.）3844号和3744号报告称，1940年9月13日下午2时50分，一行约八名日本人由一名中国男子陪同访问了高等法院，他们在院内停留了约五分钟，随后乘坐三辆摩托车离开。这名显然担任该团向导的中国男子被确认为市公署律师助理 T.J. Lee 先生。
下文签署人为进一步核实所报告的市公署律师办事处代表在场一事，与市公署律师办事处联络官 Shellewell 警司进行了联系。后者在与市公署副律师 R.T. Fryer, jr. 先生商议后告知下文签署人，这些日本人是来自日本东京的司法官员，参观中国法院的事宜是通过特务副总巡 C. Akagi 先生安排的。下文签署人随即通知“A”区督察长，后者表示对此事毫不知情。
1940年9月13日下午3时25分，收到美国海军陆战队（U.S.M.C.）情报官的电话留言，报告日本人访问高等法院一事，并询问工部局警务处是否有关于此事的情报，对方已获知警方调查的结果。

此致，
敬礼，
D. I.

Sir,

I beg to report that at 11.05 a.m. 21-8-40, a m/car
bearing S.D.F. Licence plate No. 301, stopped at the
entrance to the 2nd Branch of the Kiangsu High Court on
Wei Hai Wei Road, two male Japanese in civilian clothing
alighted from the car and approached C.P.C. 1913, who
was on duty at the entrance and speaking in Peking dia-
lect, asked the Police officer if the 1st S.S.D. Court
situated on Chekiang Road had been transferred to the
2nd Branch of the Kiangsu High Court, as per report
appearing in the Foreign Press, the C.P.C. stated that
he had no knowledge on the subject, the Japanese then
re-entered the car and drove away in a western direction

C.P.C.1913 attached to Chengtu Road Stn.
D.I. Hill
Ch. Rd. Stn.        21-8-40        Clerk Weng.

I am C.P.C. 1913 attached to Chengtu Road Station.
At 11.05 a.m. 21-8-40, I was on duty at the 2nd Branch
of the Kiangsu High Court No. 22/155 Wei Hai Wei Road., when a
m/car bearing S.D.F. Licence plate No. 301, stopped on Wei Hai
Wei Road at the entrance to Lane 155 nearby where I was standing,
I saw two Japanese alight from the car, they were wearing civil-
lian clothing, they approached me, and one of them speaking
Peking dialect, spoke as follows:- "What is the meaning of the
term 2nd Branch of the Kiangsu High Court?, has the 1st Special
District Court at Chekiang Road removed here today?" I told
the Japanese that I did not know, the Japanese then said "The
news has appeared in the Foreign press that the 1st Special
District Court in Chekiang Road will be removed to this address".
The Japanese did not converse further on the subject, but re-
entered the car and drove away in a western direction along
Wei Hai Wei Road.

Signed:

成都路警察局        1940年8月21日        文员 Weng。

我是隶属成都路警察局的华捕巡警1913号。
1940年8月21日上午11时05分，我正在威海卫路22/155号江苏高等法院第二分院执勤，此时一辆悬挂特别市财政局（S.D.F.）牌照第301号的汽车停在威海卫路靠近我站立处的155弄入口附近，我看见两名日本人从车上下来，他们身穿便服，向我走来，其中一人用北京话说道：“‘江苏高等法院第二分院’这个名称是什么意思？浙江路的第一特区地方法院今天搬到这里了吗？”我告诉该日本人我不知道，该日本人随后说：“外文报纸上刊登消息说，浙江路的第一特区地方法院将迁至此地址”。该日本人未就此话题继续交谈，而是重新上车，沿威海卫路向西驶离。

Date December 20, 1939.
Subject Gaol of the Shanghai Second Special District Court - clerical
staff and other employees demanding allowances.
Made by D. I. Pan Lien rik Forwarded by D. I. Bradford

About two months ago, some 140 members
of the Gaol of the Shanghai Second Special
District Court, Rue Massenet, French Concession,
submitted a demand to the court authorities
for an allowance of $15 each per month due to
the high cost of living and the President
applied to the Ministry of Justice for instructions.
No reply has yet been received from the Ministry,
and the employees on December 19 requested the
assistance of Mr. Yang Pang (杨邦), President
of the 3rd Branch of the Kiangsu High Court,
who agreed to petition the Ministry of Justice
to issue instructions as soon as possible.
A temporary allowance would be given at the end
of December if no reply is received from the
Ministry by that time. These employees are
working as usual.

Pan Lien-pik
D. I.

D. C. (Special Branch)

制作人 D. I. Pan Lien rik 转呈人 D. I. Bradford

大约两个月前，位于法租界马思南路（Rue Massenet）的上海第二特区地方法院监狱的约140名成员，因生活成本高昂，向院方当局提出每人每月发放15元津贴的要求，院长遂向司法部请示。截至目前尚未收到司法部的回复，雇员们于12月19日请求江苏高等法院第三分院院长杨邦（Yang Pang）先生协助，杨先生同意尽快 petition 司法部发出指示。如果届时仍未收到司法部的回复，将在12月底发放临时津贴。这些雇员目前照常工作。

Pan Lien-pik
D. I.

Two Male Japanese Subjects visit the Kiangsu High Court situated at 22/155 Wei Hai Wei Rd.

At 1.12 p.m. 25-11-39 a black Ford 5 seater Car, bearing S.M.C. Lic. No. 5284 which was driven by a Chinese, who is assumed to be a chauffeur, stopped at a point on Wei Hai Wei Road opposite the entrance to Lane No. 155 Wei Hai Wei Road.

EMPLOYEES OF CHINESE COURTS IN SHANGHAI LODGE
COMPLAINT WITH CHUNGKING GOVERNMENT RELATING
TO THEIR TREATMENT

Dissatisfaction due to the
falling value of legal tender notes and the high cost
of living has been growing among the employees of the
Chungking Government Courts and Gaols in Shanghai.
Recently the Court gaol authorities have been faced
with difficulty in purchasing foodstuffs for prisoners
because merchants who have been supplying foodstuffs to
the gaols have become disinterested in the business.
For this reason, the entire staff sent a letter of
protest to the Chungking Government. The employees
of the Shanghai Special District Court Gaol and of the
Kiangsu High Court Gaol in the French Concession are
reported to have sent a joint letter to the Ministry of
Justice of the Chungking Government asking for better
treatment.

Yang Fong, representative of
the Second Special District Court Gaol is reported to
have sent a letter to the Chungking Government asking
it to remit funds urgently because no merchants wish to
supply food to the Gaol which is now receiving assistance
from the French authorities.

TAIRIKU SHIMPO

ILLOGICAL ARGUMENT OF BRITISH AUTHORITIES ON
THEIR PROTECTION OF NATIONAL GOVERNMENT'S
COURTS

In connection with the question
of trespass upon the buildings of the First Special
District Court committed by the British Defence Force in
Shanghai, great interest has been aroused in various
quarters.

The British authorities advanced
the argument that it was natural for the British Defence
Force to undertake the guarding of the Court
because it is situated within the British sector. Yet
it is strange that no guards have been placed at the
Second Kiangsu High Branch Court at No. 149 Weihaiwei
Road although this Court is located within the American
sector. If the stationing of soldiers in the building
of the Court is justifiable the American Defence Force
would have dispatched soldiers to the Court for the same
reason as that advanced by the British authorities. On
August 9 the American Defence Force posted only one
soldier at the Court's gate. Judging by the foregoing,
the stationing of guards at the First Special District Court
constitutes an arbitrary action on the part of the
British Defence Force and must have been taken in
co-operation with the Chungking Government.

Local Japanese residents hope
that their authorities will adopt strong measures against
such deliberate assistance to the Chiang Kai Shek regime
by the British authorities in an occupied area.

英国当局为其保护国民政府法院所作之不合逻辑的辩解

关于驻沪英军防卫部队侵入第一特区法院大楼一事，各方极为关注。

英国当局提出辩称，鉴于该法院位于英方防区内，由英军防卫部队负责守卫乃自然之举。然而奇怪的是，位于美方防区内的威海卫路149号江苏高等法院第二分院却未派驻警卫。如果向法院大楼派驻士兵是正当的，那么美军防卫部队也会以英国当局提出的同样理由向法院派遣士兵。8月9日，美军防卫部队仅在法院大门处派驻了一名士兵。综上所述，在第一特区法院派驻警卫构成英军防卫部队的专断行为，且必定是与重庆政府合作采取的举动。

Chinese-American Daily News (Editorial) :-

The Position of the Special District Courts

After the withdrawal of the Chinese forces from Shanghai and vicinity, followed by the fall of Nanking, many organizations of the so-called "Reformed Government" made their appearance one after another in the local Foreign Settlements. The Shanghai Maritime Customs and the Chinese Post Office could not maintain their original stand. However, the Courts in the Foreign Settlements have been in existence independently and there is much significance in this.

Using the name of a certain organization, a certain Chinese named Lin (林) attempted unsuccessfully to take over the Shanghai First Special District Court in the spring of last year. In the spring of this year, Fu Siao-en, Mayor of the Shanghai City Government, sent a letter to the S.M.C. demanding the return of the Court. We know here that Japan has for a long time been doing her utmost to seize the Courts in the Foreign Settlements. Realizing the importance of the Courts, the authorities of the Foreign Settlements refrained from co-operating with her, resulting in the present impasse. However, Japan has not forsaken her ambition. Some time ago, the local Japanese Consul-General submitted demands to the British and American Consuls-General and the Chairman of the S.M.C. for the reorganization of the S.M.C. and the retrocession of the Special District Courts. It was recently reported that a demand had been submitted to the French authorities for the transfer of the Shanghai Second Special District Court.

The Special District Court in the International Settlement was reorganized in 1930 from the Provisional Court after the abolition of the Mixed Court, an agreement being signed by the National Government and the interested Powers. Therefore any change of this Court must be made according to the agreement. Japan has no right to demand the Powers concerned to alter the constitution of the Court since she is not one of

《中美日报》（社论）：

特区法院的地位

随着中国军队从上海及周边地区撤退，继而南京沦陷，所谓“维新政府”的许多组织相继在当地外国租界内出现。上海海关和中国邮政无法维持其原有立场。然而，外国租界内的法院一直独立存在，此事意义重大。

去年春天，一名姓林（Lin）的中国人借某组织之名，企图接管上海第一特区法院，但未成功。今年春天，上海市政府市长傅筱庵致函工部局，要求归还法院。我们由此得知，日本长期以来一直竭力夺取外国租界内的法院。外国租界当局意识到法院的重要性，拒绝与其合作，导致目前的僵局。然而，日本并未放弃其野心。此前，当地日本总领事向英美总领事及工部局总董提出要求，重组工部局并交还特区法院。近日有报道称，已向法国当局提出要求，移交上海第二特区法院。

国际租界内的特区法院于1930年由临时法院改组而成，当时废除了会审公廨，并由国民政府与相关列强签署了协定。因此，对该法院的任何变更必须依据协定进行。日本无权要求相关列强改变法院的体制，因为她并非

page_data.en:
the signatories to the agreement, which expired on
March 31, 1939. As the parties have not indicated
their desire for a revision or abolition of the agreement,
it continues in effect, whilst the signatories cannot
now present a demand to the National Government for a
reorganization of the Court. The "Reformed Government",
which is not recognized by the signatories of this
agreement, is not in a position to interfere with the
question. In fulfilling their duty to protect the
Court, the signatories of the agreement should try to
maintain the independence of the Court should a third
party attempt to interfere illegally with its administration.
The reason given by the Japanese Consul-General
for taking over the Special District Courts is that
the Judges of these Courts have been appointed by the
Chungking Government and that the Chungking Government
has no actual power in Shanghai. As the Powers of the
signatories of the Court rendition agreement have so far
treated the National Government as the only Chinese
Government, it is natural that the Judges of the Courts
should be appointed by the National Government. If
the Judges should be appointed by the puppet organization,
it would mean that the Powers of the signatories recognize
this organization as a de facto Government.
The local Foreign Settlements are not
Japanese occupied areas and the power of the National
Government over the Special District Courts is still
complete and it may continue to exercise its power over
the Courts. So long as the sovereign rights of the
National Government exist, the signatories of the Court
rendition agreement have to recognize it as the legal
Chinese Government.

该协定的签字国之一，该协定已于1939年3月31日到期。由于各方未表示希望修订或废除该协定，协定继续有效，而签字国目前也不能向国民政府提出重组法院的要求。未获本协定签字国承认的“维新政府”无权干涉此问题。在履行保护法院的职责时，若有第三方试图非法干涉其行政管理，协定签字国应努力维护法院的独立性。
日本总领事提出接管特区法院的理由是，这些法院的法官由重庆政府任命，而重庆政府在上海没有实权。由于《法院交还协定》签字国的列强迄今为止一直视国民政府为唯一的中国政府，法院法官由国民政府任命乃是自然之事。如果法官由傀儡组织任命，则意味着签字国列强承认该组织为事实上的政府。
当地外国租界并非日本占领区，国民政府对特区法院的权力仍然完整，并可继续行使其对法院的权力。只要国民政府的主权存在，《法院交还协定》的签字国就必须承认其为合法的中国政府。
